articles.title: Williams sisters’ US Open return ends in heartbreak with third-set tie-break defeat
articles.summary: American duo lose 6-3, 6-7(6), 7-6(7) to Maya Joint and Chan Hao-ching. Serena and Venus crash out of women’s doubles in first round. In the end, after so much toil and admirable fight, defeat came swiftly for one of the greatest doubles teams to ever share a tennis court.
body: They came close. The Williams sisters had clawed their way back into the match after trailing a 1-4 in their final set against Chan Hao-ching and Maya Joint, and they established a 5-0 lead in the third set tie-break. Just as they appeared to be on the verge of victory, they were brushed aside, losing 6-3, 6-7 (6), 7-6 (7) in the first round of the US Open.

This was one of the few times in recent tennis history where a player’s doubles appearance seemed far more important than their singles contributions. While the 44-year-old Serena had opted out of taking a singles wildcard for the US Open after suffering a knee injury during her singles comeback at Wimbledon in July against Joint, the 46-year-old Venus lost in the singles first round here to Sofia Kenin, her 15th consecutive singles loss. No matter, from the moment it became clear that the Williams sisters were aiming to compete alongside each other in doubles again, this was the match that people wanted to see.

articles.title: Former world champion Ruiz Jr loses comeback fight
articles.summary: American heavyweight Andy Ruiz Jr, who shocked Anthony Joshua in 2019 to take his world titles, loses comeback fight to Poland's Damian Knyba.
body: The 36-year-old heavyweight shocked the boxing world seven years ago by beating Britain's Anthony Joshua to take his world titles.
Ruiz Jr has since been beset by injuries and was taking part in just his fourth fight since losing the rematch to Joshua in December 2019.

He looked a shadow of his former self at the Prudential Center in Newark, saved by the bell after scrambling back to his feet following a knockdown in the seventh, he eventually lost by a unanimous points decision.
Judges scored the fight 117-110, 114-113 and 114-113 in favour of the Pole, who took his record to 18 wins and one defeat, but Ruiz Jr was quick to demand a rematch.

articles.title: Cameron Myers shines in star-studded field to win 1500m at Diamond League final
articles.summary: Australian beats Olympic champs Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Cole Hocker. Pole vaulter Kurtis Marschall soars over 5.82m to finish third in Brussels. Middle-distance runner Cameron Myers has become only the eighth Australian to win a Diamond League final crown with victory in the men’s 1500m in Brussels.
body: The 20-year-old claimed one of the biggest wins of his career to date as he beat a star-studded field that included Olympic champions Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Cole Hocker to continue his own meteoric rise.
Myers timed a late burst down the home straight to perfection and dipped at the line to snatch victory in 3:30.14 ahead of Kenya’s Phanuel Kipkosgei Koech (3:30.18).
Ingebrigtsen, on the comeback trail after achilles surgery in February, dictated the pace of the race and looked on course for a morale-boosting win before ​ tiring in the last 30 metres.
America’s Ethan Strand edged past the Norwegian in the final few steps to cross the line in 3:30.50 and round out the podium.

articles.title: Williams sisters exit US Open but excite - what does future hold?
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams may have lost in their US Open doubles return, but the veteran pair proved they can still compete on an entertaining night in New York.
body: Rarely has a women's doubles first-round match headlined the US Open night session - but the Williams sisters are like no other pairing.
Serena and Venus Williams might have a combined age of 90, but their star remains undimmed. As does their ability to compete at the highest level when they are in tandem.

Even though the superstar siblings - aged 44 and 46 - lost on their highly anticipated Grand Slam return, their performance in a narrow defeat by 14th seeds Chan Hao-ching and Maya Joint led to an entertaining night in New York.
A packed Arthur Ashe Stadium roared on the American icons as they looked on course for a memorable win - but ultimately fell short in a 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (10-7) loss.

articles.title: How bullying led Britain's Campbell to the UFC
articles.summary: Introduced to combat sports as a seven-year-old after being bullied at school, Kurtis Campbell is now chasing success in the UFC.
body: Kurtis Campbell was only seven years old when his parents decided something drastically needed to change.
During his time at primary school in Liverpool, Campbell was targeted by bullies. His parents, Jay and Michelle, could see the effect it was having.
It was then that they signed him up for Muay Thai classes to help him learn how to defend himself.
"From there, I've never looked back," Briton Campbell told BBC Sport. "I've been in love with the sport ever since."

articles.title: LA Clippers fans answer if Kawhi Leonard deserves a tribute video after controversial exit
articles.summary: The Kawhi Leonard era came to a crashing end for the Los Angeles Clippers. When the Los Angeles Clippers welcomed Kawhi Leonard to the roster in 2019, the expectation was to win multiple NBA Championships.
body: However, it took just seven years for the dream to shatter as Leonard was traded to the Toronto Raptors after the NBA found him guilty in the salary cap circumvention scandal.
Leonard is gone, but let’s not forget that he still helped the team reach the Western Conference Finals for the first time in franchise history during the 2021 NBA Playoffs.

Of course, Leonard’s past several seasons have been plagued with injuries. Combining these facts makes it a huge debate about whether Kawhi deserves a tribute video from the Clippers when he returns to Intuit Dome next season.
“For what? They won 3 series with him,” a fan wrote. While another added, “Uncle Dennis gets one.”

articles.title: Erasmus and Rennie's war of words escalates ahead of third Test
articles.summary: The four-match series is finely poised at 1-1, with Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry seemingly reaching new heights of tension as Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie’s war of words escalates.
body: Picture the scene: The touring All Blacks win the opening Test with a 33-16 at Ellis Park. Then, the Springboks hit back with a thrilling 33-26 victory over New Zealand in Cape Town.

Named in the front row for the Springboks for that contest were Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw. Just one hour before kick-off, that was changed to Gerhard Steenekamp, Deon Fourie and Thomas du Toit with the original three dropping to the bench.
Erasmus said this was down to conditions and a chance of rain not materialising.
"We thought it was going to be wet and that's why we picked the front row, Erasmus said after the match. "The whole weather prediction, the whole week, was it was going to be wet."

articles.title: Jaissle hails Newcastle’s brave bet on youth after summer overhaul and £51m swoop for Fernandez-Pardo
articles.summary: Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle has said the club have been brave with their recruitment this summer. Newcastle have had a summer of transition, with Jaissle arriving as head coach and a host of senior players leaving St James' Park.
body: Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali were all sold for large fees, while Nick Woltemade and Kieran Trippier have also departed.
Newcastle have focused on emerging talent in the summer window, making eight permanent signings that are all aged 24 or under.
Speaking ahead of today's clash with Bournemouth, Jaissle said the club have been bold in placing so much faith in young talent.
"Real clear idea on all the signings, a young squad in general. Young with huge potential. It's a brave way, but the way we want to go in Newcastle, we are fully committed to working with the lads."

It was Saints' seventh defeat in their last 10 matches and second heavy loss in a row, having suffered a 28-point reverse to Leeds a week ago.

O'Carroll is due to be replaced by former Brisbane Broncos and Australia head coach Kevin Walters ahead of the 2027 season, and the experienced coach will hope to galvanise the Saints back to their best next season.
But eyebrows have been raised over the team's recruitment decisions this year, with the club also struggling with a big injury crisis. At one stage in July, 16 players were sidelined with injuries.

articles.title: Greaves makes more history with win at Czech Darts Open
articles.summary: Beau Greaves made more darting history as she became the first woman to win a match on the PDC's European Tour - a feat that secured her a second-round clash with Luke Humphries at the Czech Darts Open.
body: The 22-year-old rallied from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in Prague on Friday night and will now play world No 2 Humphries in the last-32 on Saturday evening, with the winner meeting Nathan Aspinall or Andrew Gilding in round three on Sunday afternoon.

Greaves' latest landmark moment follows becoming the first woman to hit a nine-darter on the PDC Pro Tour, against Mensur Suljovic back in February, and the first to win a PDC ranking title, doing so when she edged Michael Smith 8-7 at Players Championship 11.
She was also the first woman to qualify for a European Tour event when she reached last month's Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Greaves lost to Rob Cross in the first round in Budapest despite averaging 104 but her run in Prague will now last at least one more match after pinning double one to defeat Gurney, a player she had suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to in round one of the 2026 World Championship.
